## Understand + Decide (2026-07-20)

**Understand team:** Plan (authoritative truth) + rust-engineer (exhaustive git-grep inventory) + research-analyst (derived artifacts/CI) + multi-agent-coordinator. Map: scratchpad `ub-lp9.15-understand-map.md`; line-level inventory: `ub-lp9.15-drift-inventory.md`.

### Key findings (orchestrator-verified on disk, not just relayed)

1. **The task brief understated the problem: the AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE is itself stale (T0).** `docs/PRD.md` has **11 stale sites**, incl. D28's consequences list (`:111`) still asserting the pre-D41 mapping `shared state (v1.2), planning (v1.3), streamable-HTTP (v1.4), TUI (v1.5)` with **no forward-amendment marker**. Verified verbatim. T0 must land FIRST — any derivative sweep otherwise re-derives from a false source.
2. **`docs/roadmap.html` is ALREADY D41-correct** (refreshed by `78760f1`). Tier T4 is empty, not pending — the brief's "also refresh roadmap.html" is already done.
3. **`docs/PROCESS.md` is OUT of the doc-lint corpus** — yet it is `@`-imported into every session, so its stale `until the v1.2 shared remote` (`:103`) has the highest blast radius per byte in the repo and zero mechanical protection.
4. **No CI class fires on product-version prose.** doc_lint class (b) needs an FR/NFR-adjacent `[marker]`; class (e) only checks that a `§N` *resolves* — so the ~14 cross-refs pointing at the WRONG existing section are invisible to the lint. "The lint will catch it later" is not available.
5. **Corpus correction:** `xtask/src/doc_lint.rs:29` CORPUS = **19 files** incl. all 12 crate plans (a prior session note claiming 2 files was wrong; corrected).
6. **Traps a `sed` would hit:** the streamable-HTTP item must be **rewritten to v2+/unscheduled, never renumbered** (D41 removed it from committed versions; renumbering asserts a false "v1.5 streamable-HTTP"); `unblock.mcp.v1.N` / `unblock.scheduler.vN` / `--tlsv1.2` / Cargo.lock are NOT drift; `unblock-policy.md:24` + `unblock-render.md:33` "no v1.2 participation" are **doubly wrong** (number moved AND roadmap §9 marks both ◐ at v1.2).

### Canonical D41 mapping (settled — all three scouts agreed, verified vs roadmap §8/§9)
planning v1.3→**v1.2** (§4→§3) · shared-state v1.2→**v1.3** (§3→§4) · TUI v1.5→**v1.4** (§6→§5) · scale v1.4→**v1.5** (§5→§6) · streamable-HTTP v1.4→**v2+ unscheduled** (§7). v1/v1.1 unchanged; new **v1.0.1 [PLANNED]** slot.

### Miguel's fork resolutions — MAXIMAL on all four
- **E1 README scope → (b) FULL**, incl. the 3 lines inside the dated 2026-06-19 consistency report. Rejects the dated-record convention.
- **E2 the 132 derivative rows → (b) FULL SWEEP NOW** of all 12 crate plans + Rust doc-comments. **PROCESS §3's zero-live-hits checklist governs over §2's just-in-time** for a decision-change cascade. (The 3 carve-outs are subsumed.)
- **E3 PRD D28 → in-place REWRITE** (not a forward-amendment marker). Coherent with E1. The streamable-HTTP caveat still binds: rewrite to v2+, do not renumber.
- **E4 v1.0.1 → first-class**: define the `PLANNED` status in §0, fix the status line `:3`, **and add a v1.0.1 column to both matrices §8 and §9**.

**Orchestrator call (obvious default, not a fork):** `.unblock/issues.jsonl:3` — a CLOSED issue's historical description — is left as-is. Rewriting tracker history for a closed issue is not doc reconciliation, and an issue description is never authoritative anyway.

**Scope:** ~29 files, ~166 rows. Next: Spec/Plan (4 parallel spec writers) → design Review gate (≥3 adversarial).

## Spec/Plan + design Review gate (2026-07-20) — **GATE: FAIL → remediated**

**Spec team:** 4 parallel changeset writers (T0 PRD+roadmap · T1/T2 contract docs · T3a 6 big crate plans · T3b 6 remaining + Rust). **Review gate:** 3 adversarial lenses (conformance/truth · mechanical safety · completeness) + coordinator. Report: scratchpad `ub-lp9.15-review-gate.md`; changesets `spec-*.md` (~210 blocks).

### Verdict: FAIL as submitted — 3 BLOCKER / 4 MAJOR / 6 MINOR (21 raw findings → 13 distinct). All 7 MUST-FIX + 8/10 SHOULD-FIX patched into the changesets in place; coordinator ruled no re-gate required for the patched set.

### The three blockers
- **M7 (root cause) — ORCHESTRATOR SCOPE-PARTITION BUG.** `docs/plans/implementation-plan.md` and `docs/plans/ci-cd-and-distribution.md` — **corpus entries 6 and 7** of the 19-file doc-lint corpus — were assigned to **no changeset** and not even listed as verified-clean. Both carried live stale hits. My partition, my defect; the completeness lens caught it by re-running the sweep independently instead of trusting the inventory.
- **M1 — `implementation-plan.md:93`** `roadmap §6` → `§5`. TRAP 3: D31's write-lock/co-tenancy text is at `00-roadmap.md:339-347`, inside `## 5. v1.4 TUI`; post-D41 `§6` is Scale. **Invisible to doc-lint class (e)** because `§6` still resolves. Adjudicated against the completeness lens (which called it a possibly-frozen record) on the evidence that the roadmap's own internal refs to the same D31 material were updated in the D41 pass.
- **M3 — `ci-cd-and-distribution.md:58`** `tested target (v1.2)` → `(v1.3)`. Severity raised to BLOCKER: a live stale hit inside a corpus file defeats E2's zero-live-hits AC outright.

### The most valuable single finding
**M4 — `unblock-storage.md:120` (OQ-6): a STANCE defect, not a numbering one.** The specced renumber would have emitted "a **v1.3** design decision that lands in `remote.rs`" — **re-committing into v1.3 a decision the roadmap records as DROPPED** (`00-roadmap.md:255-256`: multi-writer reconciliation LWW-vs-oplog, moot under the primary-serialized write contract, deferred to the Turso Sync v2+ candidate). Found by **one lens alone**; the other two swept the file clean because they checked the version-token and §-ref axes, and this defect lives on the *stance* axis. Third TRAP-5 sibling after `fuzz.md:87` and `engine.md:114`.

### Other notable
- **M5** — one block out of ~210 was malformed (two consecutive `NEW:` lines); a first-/last-wins applier would have half-applied it, and the OLD line vanishes cleanly either way → **invisible loss**. Re-emitted as a single fenced NEW.
- **M6** — the v1.0.1 matrix cells framed the comment bug as "validation/deserialization"; `ub-lp9.12` says the root cause is **undiagnosed**, and that framing also implies a surface change the same block denies. Neutralised.
- Spec writers corrected the inventory in several places (disk wins): PRD has **19** sites, not ~11 (`:111` carries 3, `:113` carries 5); `docs/plans/README.md` real edits are **8**, not 17 (12 of the counted rows are body cells needing no edit).

### Orchestrator rulings on the two unpatched SHOULD-FIX
- **S9** (README `:119` header stamp says D37/2026-07-17 while its body now embeds D41/2026-07-20) → **APPLY**, routed to the T1/T2 implementer.
- **S10** (`README.md:97` shows `unblock-cli (—)` where roadmap §9 marks it `◐`; same for health/engine/mcp/fuzz) → **OUT OF SCOPE, follow-up filed.** It **predates D41** (that column was the shared-state release before the relabel), so it is not D41 drift, and re-syncing the table's glyphs to §9 is precisely the table-rebuild option **(c)** Miguel did **not** choose in E1. Pulling it in would smuggle back the scope he rejected.

**Next:** Implement — 4 implementers in isolated worktrees over disjoint file sets, each committing its own branch. Shared tree verified clean at `21d40db` == `origin/main` before launch.

## Implement + Verify quality gate (2026-07-20) — **VERIFY GATE: PASS**

**Implement:** 4 implementers in isolated worktrees over disjoint file sets; **zero `OLD`-match failures across ~210 blocks**; each ran doc-lint green in its own worktree. Integrated by cherry-pick onto `ub-lp9.15-d41-doc-reconcile` — 4 atomic Conventional Commits, **28 files, +236/−232**.

**Verify team:** code-reviewer (truth-of-result) · qa-expert (completeness + regression) · rust-engineer (code safety + contract integrity) + coordinator. Report: scratchpad `ub-lp9.15-verify-gate.md`.

### Verdict: PASS — 0 BLOCKER, conditional on 3 fixes (all landed, see below)

### Full CI probe (orchestrator-run, per-job exit codes captured)
`fmt` exit 0 · `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` exit 0, **0 warnings** · `test --workspace --locked` **113 suites / 1366 passed / 0 failed** · `insta --check` no snapshots to review, zero `.snap.new` · `doc-lint` OK (19 docs, 6 classes clean) · `check-layering` OK (NFR-15 conforms).

**Probe methodology correction, recorded because it nearly mattered:** my first probe piped the test section through `tail -25` and reported the exit code of the trailing `echo`. It showed "5 tests passed" and exit 0 — i.e. a green verdict resting on ~0.4% of the suite. Re-run with explicit per-job exit capture. A truncated probe that *looks* green is worse than a red one.

### The three conditional must-fixes — all verified by me on disk before applying
- **V1 — `.unblock/issues.jsonl` not re-exported** (PROCESS §6 requires it in the same commit). Landed with this comment thread.
- **V2 — `CLAUDE.md:23`** `v1/v1.1 LOCKED; v1.2–v1.5/v2+ PROPOSED.` → adds `v1.0.1 PLANNED`. **Notable defect class:** the spec writer's "CLAUDE.md is zero-stale" finding was *correct* on the version→theme axis. The line became incomplete because of **our own E4 change** — we minted the v1.0.1 slot, and CLAUDE.md's summary row didn't know about it. Undetectable by any pre-change sweep; only a post-change read finds it.
- **V3 — `crates/unblock-sync/src/error.rs:86`** read `used at v1.3 reconciliation`. Roadmap `:255-256` records multi-writer reconciliation as **dropped as a v1.3 question**. The mechanical v1.2→v1.3 renumber *manufactured* a falsehood that did not exist before. **4th TRAP-5 sibling** (after fuzz.md:87, engine.md:114, storage.md OQ-6) and again caught by **one lens only**.

### Coordinator residual risk — converted from inference to proof
The Verify coordinator flagged that its "pre-existing vs newly-introduced" reasoning was *inferred* (its role has no Bash) and asked for `git show main:...` confirmation. I ran it: `### v1*` heading counts are **identical on main vs branch** across all 7 files (policy 4/4, render 3/3, config 3/3, model 4/4, storage 4/4, engine 2/2, mcp 0/0) — no section was added or removed, only renumbered. **The inference was correct**, so the downgrade of lens-1 findings #1/#2 to SHOULD-FIX stands.

### Dismissals worth recording
- Lens 1 #3 (reframe §8:436 as a "validation fix") **rejected** — it would contradict roadmap:80 and reinstate exactly what design-gate M6 stripped. But the lens was right that `ub-lp9.12`'s actual remedy is "return a structured error", and the owning doc is roadmap §1:79-80 → filed separately rather than smuggled in here.
- Lens 1 #7 (`impl-plan:106`) — frozen T3.9 history for a pre-GA task; editing it corrupts the record.
- Lens 2 findings on archived `ub-lp9.10` strings — immutable audit record.

### Follow-ups filed rather than scope-crept
`ub-lp9.16` (README crate-table glyph divergence vs roadmap §9, gate finding S10). Two more from Verify SHOULD-FIX to file: the roadmap §1:79-80 comment-bug remedy wording, and `unblock-storage.md:41`'s `v1.1→v1.5` stability rule which excludes the new v1.0.1 migration.

`docs/plans/README.md`'s per-crate table disagrees with the roadmap §9 crate-impact matrix on participation glyphs. Known site: `:97` shows `unblock-cli (—)` where roadmap §9 marks cli as participating; the T1/T2 spec writer also flagged health/engine/mcp/fuzz mismatches.

So it is not D41 drift. More importantly, re-syncing the table's contents to §9 IS the "rebuild the table as a mirror of roadmap §9" option (E1 option (c)) that Miguel explicitly declined; doing it inside ub-lp9.15 would have smuggled back rejected scope.

NOTE the standing tension this sits on: `docs/plans/README.md:100` already declares `00-roadmap.md` §3-§7 + the §9 crate-impact table AUTHORITATIVE over this per-crate table. So a reader following the hierarchy is not misled on a decision — which is exactly why this is P3, not urgent.

Option (b) is worth real consideration — the whole reason :100 exists is that this table duplicates something authoritative.

description:
Split out of ub-lp9.15 as a Verify-gate SHOULD-FIX (lens 1 finding #3, partially upheld).

`docs/plans/00-roadmap.md` §1 (~:79-80) describes the v1.0.1 comment-add fix as making the comment "durably stored". But `ub-lp9.12` — the issue that owns the bug — specifies the remedy as making a malformed / missing-required `comment add` **return a structured VALIDATION_FAILED error**, i.e. REJECT the payload, not persist it.

Those are opposite behaviours for the same input. As written the roadmap is a live prescription to persist a payload that ub-lp9.12 says should be rejected — which is the more dangerous direction, since the whole bug is that a malformed payload silently succeeded.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN ub-lp9.15: that task reconciled version NUMBERING to D41. This is a statement about REMEDY BEHAVIOUR that happens to sit in the same file — a different defect class, and one that touches what v1.0.1 actually ships. It also overlaps the design-gate M6 ruling, which deliberately stripped "validation/deserialization" framing from the v1.0.1 matrix cells on the grounds that ub-lp9.12 records the root cause as UNDIAGNOSED. Any fix here must stay consistent with M6: describe the remedy without asserting a root cause nobody has established yet.

DECIDE: does the roadmap wording follow ub-lp9.12 (reject with a structured error), or does ub-lp9.12's remedy need revisiting first? Read ub-lp9.12 before editing either.
title: roadmap §1:79-80 states the comment-bug remedy as durable storage, not a structured error

description:
Split out of ub-lp9.15 as a Verify-gate residual-risk item (#3).

`docs/plans/crates/unblock-storage.md:41` states a schema-stability rule scoped to the range "v1.1 → v1.5". D41 minted a NEW v1.0.1 maintenance slot that sits BELOW v1.1, and one of its three items (ub-lp9.13) is precisely a **forward migration for the comments schema**. So the rule's range excludes the one release that is known to carry a migration.

Harmless today — v1.0.1 is PLANNED, not being built. It becomes wrong the moment v1.0.1 is actually planned, which is exactly when someone will read this rule to decide whether the migration is allowed.

FIX: extend the range to include v1.0.1, or restate the rule in terms that do not enumerate versions at all (preferable — the enumeration is what rotted). Note the second option is the same rot-proofing that ub-lp9.15 applied to docs/PROCESS.md:103, which was rewritten from a bare version number to a named release + roadmap § pointer.

`docs/plans/crates/unblock-storage.md` is one of the 19 doc-lint corpus files (`xtask/src/doc_lint.rs:29`).
